question: The idiom 'Token strike' implies:
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**, i.e. Warning strike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Token strike"** refers to a brief and symbolic protest action, usually intended as a warning rather than a full-fledged strike. (प्रतीकात्मक हड़ताल)

 
 
• **Example:** The workers initiated a token strike to draw attention to their demands for better working conditions.
 
 
 
• **Warning strike** refers to a short-duration strike meant to signal dissatisfaction or to warn employers of possible future action. (चेतावनी हड़ताल)
 
 
• **Example:** The union called for a warning strike to pressurize the management to address their grievances.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "Token strike" aligns with the concept of a "Warning strike."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **No protest** (कोई विरोध नहीं): Indicates a situation where no action or demonstration is taken.

 
 
• **Example:** Despite the unfair policies, there was no protest from the employees.
 
 
 
• **Heavy protest** (जोरदार विरोध): Refers to a large-scale and intense protest.
 
 
• **Example:** The citizens staged a heavy protest against the new taxation laws.
 
 
 
• **Silent protest** (मूक विरोध): A form of protest where participants remain silent to express their discontent.
 
 
• **Example:** The activists organized a silent protest to oppose deforestation in the area.
